gaps.sentence: The ___ reason for the delay was the weather.
gaps.hint: adjective meaning main or most important
gaps.explanation: 'Principal' as an adjective means main or most important; 'principle' is a noun meaning a basic rule or belief.

gaps.hint: past participle after 'have'; the verb takes no object
gaps.explanation: 'Rise' (rise, rose, risen) takes no object: sales have risen. 'Raise' takes an object: they raised prices.

gaps.sentence: There is little ___ that the plan will be approved.
gaps.hint: pattern: little ___ that something will happen
gaps.explanation: 'Possibility that ...' is the standard pattern; 'opportunity' means a situation that lets you do something.

gaps.sentence: The bank agreed to ___ him the money.
gaps.hint: meaning: give temporarily (from the giver's point of view)
gaps.explanation: 'Lend' means to give something to someone temporarily; the bank lends money. A base verb is needed after 'to'.

gaps.sentence: I can still ___ the day we first met.
gaps.hint: to keep in your memory yourself
gaps.explanation: 'Remember' means to keep something in your memory; 'remind' means to make someone else remember.

gaps.sentence: I start my new ___ at the hospital on Monday.
gaps.hint: a single, countable position of employment
gaps.explanation: 'Job' is countable — one particular position; 'work' is uncountable and cannot follow 'a new'.

gaps.sentence: Look at that bird up ___ in the tree.
gaps.explanation: 'There' refers to a place; 'their' shows possession; 'they're' means 'they are'.

gaps.sentence: I couldn't ___ what he was saying because of the noise.
gaps.explanation: 'Hear' means to receive sound; 'listen' means to pay attention deliberately and needs 'to'.
